AMZN.rationale: Amazon presents a solid fundamental case with strong trajectory. Q3 2025 showed $180.2B revenue with accelerating EPS growth ($1.59→$1.68→$1.95 over three quarters). AWS is reaccelerating to 28% YoY growth in Q1 2026, driving 59% of segment profits. The business has excellent competitive positioning: dominant e-commerce (~40% US market share), #1 cloud provider (~31% market share), and a rapidly scaling advertising business (~$70B annualized). Balance sheet is healthy with $369.6B equity and modest 0.15 debt-to-equity. However, the $200B annual capex commitment is compressing free cash flow and creating legitimate investor concern about near-term returns. Valuation at 34.4x P/E sits mid-range of its 28-39x 25-26 window, neither cheap nor expensive. The FTC antitrust trial scheduled for October 2026 and EU regulatory headwinds create meaningful overhang. Near-term catalyst: Q2 earnings on July 30 with Street at $1.81 EPS could re-rate if AWS momentum continues and capex guidance clarifies. Bill Ackman and other prominent investors are adding positions, viewing the stock as undervalued relative to AI peers. Score reflects strong franchise with positive trajectory, fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation, and a modest catalyst bump from upcoming earnings.
